text:
Brandon Hagel has 13 goals in 20 games, two of them in Thursday's win in Columbus, and there is nothing fluky about it. His 12.64 expected goals (the quality of the chances he gets himself) almost exactly match the goals, and he's generating them at a higher rate than last season. The Lightning hold 65% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice.

If anything, his point total undersells him. Tampa has scored 8.4 fewer goals than those chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists, and that kind of on-ice bad luck usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey had him 16th among forwards in wins above replacement last season and in the 99th percentile for driving chances once teammates and opponents are accounted for. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the how: he's both a setup man (97th percentile in primary shot assists) and a finisher on the cross-slot passes that go in about a quarter of the time. Not bad for a 159th overall pick. His ice time has dipped almost two minutes over his last ten games, so the role is worth watching.
